title: Four Costly Signaling Mechanisms

reviewed_pages.boundary_finding: The supplied PDF contains exactly the publisher-formatted main article from title page through references. PDF p. 11 (printed 547) has a Supplementary Materials availability notice, but no supplement is embedded; PDF pp. 11–13 continue the main-article references.

source_scope: Only the supplied published main article was used: main text, Figure 1, Table 1, notes, and footnotes on one-based PDF pages 1–13 (printed 537–549). Appendix pointers, supplementary materials, replication files, external references, and the web were not used as paper-specific evidence.

direct_comparison.scope_note: Only one paper is assessed in this independent session; therefore no cross-paper winner or article-level average is produced. The table compares its four experiments while preserving categories.
direct_comparison.finding: All four experiments share the same reporting architecture and therefore the same criterion scores. Differences in substantive results do not create differences in statistical transparency. The primary versus supporting classification is kept separate.

findings: Main-text prose, Figure 1, its caption, and footnotes 30 and 32 were treated as coequal evidence.
Figure 1 earned credit for displayed group means/visual mapping but not for uncertainty construction because its error bars are unlabeled.
No regression table exists in the experimental results; no score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.
Appendix and replication pointers were recorded only as pointers and never used to fill omitted information.

direct_comparison.note: Only one paper was assigned in this independent session, so no cross-paper winner or rank is possible. A later synthesis can compare this experiment-level record to other independently assessed papers without averaging experiment classes.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes received the same evidentiary status as prose. Credit was awarded from display notes (for example, respondent analysis unit, GLMM/logit forms, state random intercepts, covariates, sample sizes, estimates, SEs and 95% intervals). No deduction was made merely because information appeared in a table. Conversely, appendix/Dataverse pointers were not treated as evidence for omitted methods or results.

source_scope: Published main article only, including main-text figures, notes, footnotes, and equations. Supplementary material, repositories, code, linked software, and external references were excluded as evidence.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment-level comparison; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.summary: Study 2 is most transparent on raw group quantities and effects because Table 2 gives cell sizes, arm means, differences, and 95% intervals. Study 3 is clearest on model form because Table 3 identifies OLS, the omitted comparator, coefficients, robust SEs, and n. Study 1 is least reconstructable statistically because exact means, contrasts, analysis n, and uncertainty are not given in Figure 2.

findings: Main-text tables, figure notes, table notes, footnotes, and prose were accorded equal evidentiary status.
Table 2 earned credit for arm means, sample sizes, difference-in-means estimates, and confidence intervals found in the display and note.
Table 3 earned credit for OLS, reference condition, robust standard errors, observations, effects, and constants found in the display and note.
No credit was withheld merely because information appeared in a display; no appendix pointer was counted as supplying omitted details.

title: Electoral Gender Quotas and Democratic Legitimacy
source_scope: Published main article only: one-based PDF pages 1–18, corresponding to printed pages 1–18. Main text, figures, tables, notes, and footnotes were eligible. Supplementary material, preregistration, Dataverse/replication files, external references, and web sources were not consulted and did not supply omitted information.

main_article_boundaries.boundary_evidence: Page 1 begins the titled APSR article; page 15 labels supplementary material as an external destination; pages 16–18 contain declarations and references, ending the PDF. No appendix is embedded.

additional_checklist.note: No additional reporting checklist was supplied; separate checklist scoring is omitted.

experiments.name: Twelve-country 3×2 city-council survey experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment: respondents in 12 countries were randomized among six vignette cells crossing council composition (three levels) with policy issue (two levels), followed by formally analyzed legitimacy outcomes. Country, issue-area, subgroup, and robustness analyses reuse this assignment and are not separate experiments.

design_map.label: Target population
design_map.value: Online adult populations in 12 established, middle- to high-income democracies across the Americas, Europe, and Australasia; nationally representative of the online population on listed demographics.

evidence.anchor: nationally representative sample of the online population
evidence.paraphrase: The intended country samples represent people with internet access, using age, race/ethnicity, gender, geography, and country-specific variables.

design_map.value: NR beyond internet access and residence in one of the 12 sampled countries.

evidence.paraphrase: The main article identifies internet access and sampled countries but does not report minimum age, residency verification, language, panel-membership, or other respondent eligibility rules; pages 6–7 were reviewed.
evidence.locator: Measuring Legitimacy Beliefs in 12 Countries; Data Collection

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, main-text tables, figures, table/figure notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Table 1 and Figures 1–5 were inspected in the PDF. Figure points/error bars were credited as displayed evidence, but undefined bars were not treated as a reported SE/CI method. Pointers to SI tables/sections, the preregistration, or replication files were not treated as evidence.
findings: Table 1 and its note supported quota-threshold definitions and case context exactly as prose could.
Figures 2–5 and notes supported outcomes, group displays, issue-specific n totals, and the presence of error bars.
Because captions do not define the error bars, no inference-method credit was inferred from customary plotting practice.
Supplementary pointers on pages 1, 5–7, 9–11, and 15 supplied no omitted implementation information.

experiments.name: 2014–2015 noncompliance-tracking study of tutela case files and complainant interviews
experiments.classification_rationale: Observational tracking and measurement study. Cases were sampled, but no treatment/manipulation was randomized; it estimates noncompliance and supplies the experimental information treatment.

direct_comparison.scope_note: This independent session contains one paper, so no cross-paper ranking is possible. The table compares its distinct randomized experiments without averaging them.

findings.summary: Strongest on treatment descriptions, explicit equations/coding, focal Ns, baseline quantities, and effects; weakest on randomization mechanics, participant flow/missingness, multiplicity, and inference computation.
Similar statistical transparency to E1, but exact support-item wording/anchors are additionally absent; its separate sample and Table 5 are otherwise clearly linked.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes in the published main article were given equal evidentiary status. Tables 1–5 and their notes supplied full credit where they unambiguously identified arms, outcomes, baselines, sample sizes, estimates, or uncertainty. Missing SE computation, allocation mechanics, flow, and missingness were not inferred. Appendix/replication pointers did not supply omitted details.

checks.result: Table 2–5 notes were used to establish omitted/reference categories exactly as prose would be.
Table 1 established arm content; Figure 4 supplied raw distribution summaries; displayed Ns and effects were credited.
Equations 1–2 plus tables were accepted as sufficient model descriptions; no redundant equation was demanded.
Pointers in footnotes 5, 12–20 and the supplementary-materials notice were recorded only as pointers, not as evidence of omitted content.
Rendered PDF pages 9–14 were visually inspected for Table 1, Figure 4, Equations 1–2, and Tables 2–5; extracted column ordering and notes matched the page images.

source_scope: Only the supplied published main article (article.pdf), including main-text prose, tables, figures, notes, and footnotes, was used. experiments.name: Embedded single-profile conjoint experiment on value disagreement

design_map.label: Outcome definitions and timing
design_map.value: Immediately after every vignette: Favorability (positive/negative, 7 points), Neighbor/social distance (happy/unhappy to have as neighbor, 5 points), House/trust (comfort with house-sitting, 5 points); all rescaled 0–1, higher favorable/trusting. Explicit primary/secondary outcome labels NR.

evidence.anchor: three questions assessing ... favorability, social distance, and trust

findings: Tables 1 and 2 received the same evidentiary status as prose and support focal behavior and competence levels.
Figure 1 and its note received full evidentiary status for plotted marginal means, contrast structure, respondent/candidate ranges, and graphical estimates.
Figure 1 did not receive credit for a defined uncertainty measure because neither the display nor its note identifies the error bars or confidence level.
Footnote 5 received full evidentiary status for linear regression and respondent-clustered standard errors, but not for an unstated model formula or marginal-quantity computation.
Pointers to supplementary materials, preregistration, and Dataverse content were recorded only as pointers and did not supply omitted evidence.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, figure notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Figures 1–2 and their notes earned credit for visible AMCE mappings, clustered inference, 95% intervals, and Ns. Appendix pointers earned no credit for omitted details. No main-text regression table exists; the figures were neither discounted nor allowed to supply information they do not show.
checked_displays: Figure 1 and note, PDF p. 8 / printed p. 1196
Figure 2 and note, PDF p. 9 / printed p. 1197
Replication results, PDF p. 11 / printed p. 1199

direct_comparison: Within this one-paper session, E1 is substantially more statistically transparent than E2 because its figures state analysis Ns, baselines, clustered inference, and 95% intervals. E2 reports focal AMCEs and SEs but omits analysis Ns, model, and dependence adjustment. Both diagnostics are too terse to reconstruct: each gives only a qualitative robustness conclusion and points outside the main article.

experiments.name: Earlier online convenience-sample pilot
experiments.classification_rationale: Pilot with no main-article outcome: it informed hypotheses, and footnote 7 directs its results to the excluded appendix.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1 and its note, Figures 1–3 and their notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 earned credit for model form, predictors, model-specific N, coefficients, and SE displays. It did not earn credit for information it does not state, including SE type, weighting, complete outcome coding, or missingness rules. Figure notes earned credit for model linkage and 84% interval level, not for unreported interval construction. Appendix pointers earned no evidence credit.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is pending.

rows.statistical_transparency: The focal logit specification and reported coefficients are reconstructable, but the full inferential implementation, outcome coding, weighting status, estimand definition, missingness, and exact stimuli are not.
The ordering manipulation is identifiable, but no outcome, analysis, sample by arm, effect, or uncertainty is reported.
Unscored category 4; the main article reports no pilot outcome.

title: Who Hosts? The Correlates of Hosting the Internally Displaced
source_scope: Published main article only: all 16 PDF pages (printed pages 1143–1158), including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Supplementary appendices, Dataverse materials, preregistrations, external references, and web sources were excluded. Appendix pointers were treated only as evidence that details were not in the main article.

main_article_boundary.start: Article title, abstract, and Introduction on PDF page 1 / printed page 1143.
main_article_boundary.end: References conclude on PDF page 16 / printed page 1158.

experiments.name: Survey-embedded 4×2 factorial hosting-appeals experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: This is the article's only manipulated randomized study and the experiment used for its policy-facing causal claim. Four appeal states were crossed with two ethnicity primes in the September 2019 household survey. Immediate, two-week, and 10-month outcomes reuse the original assignment and therefore belong to this one experiment.

design_map.label: Target population
design_map.value: Heads (or, after two unsuccessful visits, spouses) of dwellings in 15 selected villages in Mbinga South, Kalehe, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo; the study concerns potential hosting households.

evidence.anchor: aim of interviewing every household head
evidence.paraphrase: The September 2019 survey sought a census of household heads in all 15 study villages.
evidence.locator: Data and Empirical Strategy > Village Selection and Data Collection

evidence.anchor: If the head was not present
evidence.paraphrase: Enumerators returned the next day and then interviewed the spouse if the head remained absent.

design_map.label: Eligibility criteria
design_map.value: Village eligibility: adequate cellphone reception, some displaced arrivals in the prior three months, 70–250 households, an available leasable agricultural field, and safe access. Respondent age is shown as >18. Household-head/spouse substitution is reported. No separate experiment-specific exclusion rule is stated.

evidence.anchor: Twenty-one villages were found to fit the criteria
evidence.paraphrase: The article lists the village-screening criteria and reports random selection of 15 eligible villages.
evidence.locator: Village Selection and Data Collection; footnote 8

evidence.anchor: Respondent’s age (>18 years old)
evidence.paraphrase: Table 1 indicates adult respondents.

design_map.label: Recruitment procedure
design_map.value: The field team listed all households/dwellings, attempted to interview every household head, returned the next day after absence, then interviewed a spouse; consent was voluntary and verbal and there was no compensation.

evidence.anchor: drew up a list of all households and dwellings

experiments.name: Prospective household and host–IDP dyad observational analyses
experiments.classification_rationale: Tables 1–3 analyze measured household characteristics, subsequent hosting, dyadic ethnic matching, and correlates of empathy without randomized assignment of those predictors. Random selection of villages is a sampling procedure, not a treatment manipulation.

experiments.name: Qualitative follow-up interview analyses
experiments.classification_rationale: Interviews with village chiefs, hosts, hosted households, and non-hosts contextualize mechanisms and motivations. Random sampling of interview villages/households does not create an experimental contrast.

additional_checklist.note: No additional reporting checklist was supplied; no separate checklist was obtained or scored.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment
direct_comparison.statement: A cross-paper ranking is not possible in this session because only P019 was supplied. Within P019, only the primary factorial experiment is scored; no supporting or diagnostic randomized experiment was identified.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 4 earned credit for observation counts, coefficients, standard errors, fixed effects, control-block exclusions, clustering, and standardization. It did not earn credit for information the table and note do not state (estimator, coding/reference categories, weights, flow, missingness, or exact contrasts). Appendix and Dataverse pointers supplied no omitted information.

findings: Tables and their notes received the same evidentiary status as prose. Tables 1–2 earned credit for outcomes, OLS identification, reference rows, estimates, parenthetical uncertainty displays, and observation counts.

No credit was withheld merely because information appeared in a table. Conversely, table parentheses and figure bars were not assumed to be a particular SE or CI type because neither tables, notes, nor prose defined them.
Figure legends and axes were credited for named contrasts and plotted effects. Exact values and uncertainty construction were not inferred visually.

Footnotes were treated as main-article evidence. Pointers to SI (footnotes 5, 13, 15, 19–21 and others) were recorded as evidence of absence, not as evidence that omitted details were reported in scope.
The same binary standard and component logic were applied to all four randomized samples.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison only; this independent session contains one paper. Cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.summary: All four randomized samples have the same transparency profile: strong identification of factorial levels, principal outcome coding, reference categories, OLS table estimates, and analysis units; weak reporting of recruitment, allocation, exact materials, estimands, figure/STM computation, inference type, missingness, multiplicity, and robustness details. Study 2 Israel uniquely reports its two structural cell omissions; Study 2 U.S. uniquely reveals unexplained outcome-specific missingness (3,008 versus 3,013).

inventory_notes: Five separately sampled/targeted randomized experiments receive formal main-text analyses and are classified as primary experiments.
The N=1,200 post-Musk LGBTQ replication is a new randomized sample and is scored separately as category 3.
The randomized ordering of four manipulation-check labels is a response-order control inside each experiment, not a separately analyzed experimental intervention.
No category 4 pilots or category 5 observational analyses were identified as distinct studies.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: Within P023, formal experiments have similar transparency: outcomes, estimands, analysis units, coding, graphical effects, raw distributions, and scope are clear, but randomization probabilities/generation, complete model specifications, inference construction, missingness, multiplicity, and full traceability are not. The Christian experiment uniquely prints its complete arm texts. The diagnostic replication reports almost no statistical detail.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, tables, figures, table/figure notes, and footnotes were given identical evidentiary status. Figure 1 earned exact-condition credit for the Christian experiment; Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–6 earned measurement, raw-quantity, effect, uncertainty, coding, sample, and estimator credit where their content supported it. Appendix/SM pointers supplied no credit for omitted content.
examples: Figure 1 was visually inspected and credited for the Christian arm wording.
Figure 2's note was credited for binary-outcome coding, binary logit, AMEs, pooled N, and 95% CIs.
Figures 3 and 6 were credited for plotted arm-specific response distributions even though exact percentages were deferred to the SM.
Pointers to Tables S1–S22 and the Dataverse were treated only as evidence that material is absent from the permitted source.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: Within P027, the U.S. conjoint provides the clearest dependence adjustment and direct effect plot. The ordinary U.S. experiments identify simple OLS models and robust standard errors but omit per-model N, missingness rules, exact effect uncertainty, and CI construction. The U.K. replications are not reconstructable from the main article.

findings: Figure notes were treated as evidence on the same footing as prose: Figures 2–3 supplied model form, 0–1 coding, dependent-variable means, and 95% intervals; Figures 5–7 supplied estimator and inference details.
No main-text regression table exists. Pointers to Tables A4–A8 and Appendices A–D were not treated as supplying their contents.

Graphical effect estimates and confidence intervals received results credit when the plotted object was itself the effect (Figure 5); group predictions were not treated as matched uncertainty for a Cohen's d contrast (Figures 2–3).
The same missing-information standard was applied to prose and displays; no customary implementation was inferred.

Figure 1 and footnote 17 supplied decisive design evidence; Figure 6's note supplied model and simulation detail. No score was reduced because information appeared in a display rather than prose. direct_comparison.scope: One paper was supplied, so no cross-paper winner or ranking is possible. The table compares statistical transparency across its separately scored experiments.
direct_comparison.summary: The supporting group-composition experiment is clearest on arm probabilities, outcome coding, and interaction structure. The primary experiment defines its baseline contrasts and analysis unit but omits exact materials, allocation details, model implementation, named covariates, inference construction, and analysis-specific Ns. Both diagnostics lack assignment-effect estimands and numerical assignment contrasts.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent session; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.summary: Within P033, statistical transparency is highest for the conditions/estimands and displayed group quantities in the Pew split, Conversations on Issues, and Redefining Politics experiments. Across all experiments, reconstruction is chiefly blocked by absent allocation details, analysis Ns, complete specifications, and labeled SE/CI procedures. Appendix pointers received no credit.

findings: Table 1 received the same evidentiary status as prose for sample source, total N, and field year.
Figure notes received full evidentiary status for estimator names, coding, contrasts, p-values, and displayed model-based quantities.
Unlabeled graphical error bars were not treated as identified SEs or confidence intervals because neither their type nor construction is stated.
Pointers to Supplementary Material or Dataverse appendices were recorded as pointers only and did not supply omitted evidence.
The N discrepancy for Study 8 (1,998 in Table 1 versus 2,005 in text) was preserved rather than silently resolved.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given the same evidentiary status. Tables 2–5 and their notes earned credit where they made attributes, specifications, effects, standard errors, or N clear. Figure 2 earned group-quantity credit. No credit was withheld merely because evidence was in a display; conversely, appendix pointers in Figure 2/3 notes did not supply omitted main-article information.

checks.detail: Table 2 plus the printed script established all attribute levels; Tables 4–5 established coefficient rows, estimates, parenthetical SEs, and N.
Table 4/5 notes established that parentheses are standard errors and their star thresholds.
Figure 2 marginal means counted as reported group quantities; Figure 3 counted as graphical subgroup quantities.
Uniform randomization probabilities, binary outcome coding, robust SEs, clustering, weights, and missingness rules were not inferred.
Online Appendix Table 14/15 and Appendix B references were not treated as reporting their contents.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

rows.finding: Both disclose exact stimuli and the continuous CATE equation, but neither identifies the uncertainty procedure, full model implementation for every focal display, missingness rules, or complete analysis Ns. Study 2 additionally has a 1,200-versus-1,216 count inconsistency and under-specified weighting.
Both only note randomized scale order; neither reports arm allocation, an order-effect estimand, model, sample, effect, or uncertainty.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given the same evidentiary status. Figure 2 and Figure 5 earned condition-detail credit; Figures 4 and 7 earned graphical group-quantity/effect credit. Figure notes did not earn inference credit because they give only significance thresholds and point to excluded supplements. Appendix pointers were never treated as supplied information.
checks: Exact stimuli shown in figures were credited identically to prose.
Graphical means and labeled effects were credited as reported quantities.
Undefined error bars were not converted into assumed 95% confidence intervals.
Supplementary-table pointers were recorded as pointers, not evidence of omitted methods.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, tables, table notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Figure 9 earned condition-reproduction credit; Table 2 and its note earned estimator, sample-size, group-quantity, and test-direction credit. consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables, figures, table/figure notes, footnotes, and prose received equal evidentiary status. Table 1/2 notes earned credit for difference-in-means, weighting variables, confidence level, sample sizes, estimates, and intervals. They did not earn credit for details the displays omit (allocation, arm means, variance/CI construction, weight construction, or uncertainty for list–direct gaps). Figure 1/2 graphical intervals counted as uncertainty displays, while their absent numeric subgroup estimates, Ns, and model details remained missing. Appendix pointers supplied no evidence.

additional_checklist.note: No additional checklist was supplied; no separate checklist assessment was conducted.

comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; no cross-paper ranking is possible in this session.
comparison.within_paper: Lucid 1, Lucid 2, and the California experiment receive more main-text results coverage than Lucid 3–5, but all six share the same core reconstructability gaps: omitted conjoint attributes/levels, assignment probabilities and restrictions, task counts, analysis-unit detail, dependence adjustment, and exact study-level numerical effects.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were given the same evidentiary status as prose. Appendix/supplement pointers were not treated as reporting the omitted content.
consistency_audit.visual_inspection: PDF pages 10–16 were rendered and visually inspected for figure notes, axes, labels, and column layout.

statistical_transparency_comparison: Both experiments have the same transparency profile: precise vignette arms, clear respondent analysis units, plotted group means, analyzed subgroup totals, and 95% intervals, but no explicit estimand, estimator/model, weighting or adjustment specification, missing-data rules, or inference construction. Experiment 1 reports more selected numerical percentage-point contrasts; Experiment 2 chiefly reports plotted means and threshold p-values. This is an intra-paper comparison only because this independent session contains one paper.

findings: Main-text figures and their notes received the same evidentiary status as prose: figure legends supplied analyzed totals, figures supplied group means, and notes supplied outcome wording, endpoints, and the 95% confidence level.
No regression table appears in the main article. Supplementary-table pointers were recorded as pointers only and supplied no omitted methods or results.

Graphical means and confidence intervals earned evidence credit, but they did not substitute for an unstated estimator, variance procedure, confidence-interval construction, or contrast-specific uncertainty.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, equations, tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figure 1 supplied flow counts; Figure 3 and its note supplied outcomes, effect displays, confidence level, and clustering; Tables 3–4 and their notes supplied row-specific Ns, estimates, SEs, p-values, and fixed effects. No score was reduced because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose. Conversely, pointers to supplementary sections did not supply omitted details.
examples: Figure 1 credited for randomization-arm and follow-up counts.
Figure 3 note credited for 95% intervals and village clustering.
Tables 3–4 credited for numerical estimates, uncertainty, row Ns, and spillover-stratum fixed effects.
Supplementary pointers for balance, outcome items, CACE, attrition, and robustness results were not treated as evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

title: Geo-Political Rivalry and Anti-Immigrant Sentiment: A Conjoint Experiment in 22 Countries

source_scope: Published main article only, including main-text tables, figures, notes and footnotes. Supplementary appendices, Dataverse tables, preregistration, validation-survey appendix, and cited external papers were not used as evidence.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figure notes, table notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 and Figure 1 earned full credit for attributes/levels; figure notes earned credit for marginal means, 95% intervals, and respondent clustering. No score was reduced merely because evidence was graphical or tabular. Conversely, pointers to supplementary appendices or Dataverse tables supplied no omitted details.

checks.result: Table 1 was used as direct evidence for all country-of-origin levels and pairings.
Figure 1 supplied non-origin levels; Figures 1–5 and their notes supplied marginal means, intervals, and clustering.
Footnote 13 supplied the rival-versus-allied difference estimand.
Appendix, preregistration, repository, and external-study pointers were not treated as reporting the omitted content.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: Within P048, E1 is substantially more transparent than E2 and E3 because Table 5 supplies exact lists, arm means, arm Ns, and the estimate. None of the three fully reports sequence generation, missing-data rules, multiplicity/status, or a reconstructable inference procedure. E2 omits all focal numerical results; E3 omits nearly the entire design and statistical implementation.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, and footnotes were given identical evidentiary status. Table 5 earned credit for exact arms, coding, arm means, Ns, and the point estimate; the 44%–59% interval in prose earned uncertainty credit. No equation was demanded. Conversely, general references to Kish weights, an experiment, or an appendix did not earn implementation credit where linkage/details were absent.
checks: Table 5 and its note were read as evidence, not treated as secondary to prose.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison only; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: All three experiments share the same reporting architecture and nearly identical transparency scores. GMO alone fully reports its exact condition text in the main article; needle-exchange and rent-control stimuli are deferred to the appendix. Statistical reconstructability is otherwise equally limited by absent analysis Ns, treatment probabilities, inference/dependence procedures, and model-to-figure mapping.

consistency_audit.finding: Prose, equations, figures, figure notes, Table 1, Table 2, table notes, and footnotes were treated as coequal main-article evidence; no score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display.
Table 2 labels within-subject rows with β2/β3 and cross-subject rows with β4/β5, opposite Equations 1–4 and the surrounding prose (PDF p. 6, printed p. 682).
Figure 2's right-hand preference panels visually plot about 10 points (needle) and 14 points (rent), while prose reports 4 and 9 points; GMO is about 8 in both (PDF pp. 6–7, printed pp. 682–683).
Figure 4 belief-panel x axes say ‘Somewhat/Least/Most Congruent,’ while the note and methods define belief categories as accurate (PDF p. 9, printed p. 685).
Appendix pointers were recorded as pointers only and never used as evidence for omitted methods or results.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Appendix pointers were recorded but not treated as evidence.

direct_comparison.findings: Study 1 and Study 2 have the same transparency pattern: 0/5 design, 4/8 methods, 3/5 results, and 1/2 validity. consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1, Figures 1–3, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figures earned credit for displayed point estimates, confidence intervals, analysis n, OLS estimator, and reference category. Table 1 earned evidence for unstratified conditional response rates but not arm-specific means. Appendix pointers supplied no omitted evidence.

checks.finding: Credited Figures 1–3 for Study-specific estimates, 95% CIs, n, OLS, and the ambiguous-name comparison.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: The two experiments share the same principal transparency strengths (explicit difference-in-slopes estimand, analysis unit, numeric effects) and gaps (exact materials, allocation process, full estimator, missing-data rules, model N, raw arm quantities, and SE/CI construction). Authoritarianism has more complete outcome coding; Big Five more clearly reports repeated-outcome dependence and attention-check flow.

findings: Table 2 was treated as evidence for sample totals, wave content, and outcome item counts to the same extent as prose.
Figure 5, Figure 6, Figure 7, and their notes were treated as evidence for displayed estimands and 90% confidence intervals.
No credit was withheld merely because evidence appeared in a table, figure, note, or footnote.
Table/figure pointers to Online Appendix or Supplementary Information were not treated as evidence for omitted models, materials, sample sizes, or robustness results.

The main-text model descriptions plus displays did not jointly identify SE estimation, CI construction, exact analysis N, or complete treatment/outcome materials; those omissions were scored consistently for both experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes received the same evidentiary status. Table 4 earned outcome-definition and coding credit; Tables 6–9 earned estimate, sample, raw-quantity, and traceability credit. They did not earn credit for information they do not contain (for example, allocation generation, exact RI implementation, SEs/CIs, missingness, or multiplicity). Appendix pointers supplied no evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

title: Marketing Taxation? Experimental Evidence on Enforcement and Bargaining in Malawian Markets

reviewed_pages.statement: All 16 PDF pages were reviewed. Main-article text and declarations continue through page 15; references begin on page 15 and continue on page 16. Page 15 contains only a link to supplementary material, not an embedded appendix.

source_scope: Published main article only, including its main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes; all external supplements, preregistration, files, code, and references were excluded as evidence.
inventory_notes: The randomized order of two political-engagement statements (footnote 17) is a survey-administration detail with no order-effect outcome or analysis and is not treated as a distinct substantive experiment. Random selection of long-form survey respondents is sampling, not a treatment experiment.

inventory_notes: The article self-identifies two national experiments; Study 2 is focal and Study 1 preliminary.
Four separate-sample stimulus-validation/diagnostic studies are briefly described in footnotes and are scored separately as category 3.
No pilot with no reported outcome, observational analysis, or list-experiment measurement design was identified.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper session; comparison is across experiment classes, not across papers.
direct_comparison.finding: Study 2 is more transparent than Study 1 about outcomes, estimands, preregistered versus exploratory status, raw quantities, and confidence intervals. Both substantive experiments omit allocation sequence/probabilities, per-model sample accounting, complete model specifications, and missing-data rules. The four diagnostics are not statistically reconstructable from the footnote summaries.

consistency_audit.statement: Tables, figures, table/figure notes, prose and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Table 1 earned credit for its means, contrasts, N and t-test note; Figures 4–8 earned credit for displayed means/effects and 95% CIs. No credit was withheld merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, SI pointers in Figure 2 and Figures 4–8 were not treated as supplying omitted coefficients/specifications.
checks: Table 1 note used as evidence for outcome scale, N, and two-tailed t-tests.
Figure notes used as evidence for OLS labels, contrast direction, and 95% confidence intervals.
Visual inspection confirmed Figures 1 and 3 show the factorial task structures.
External SI/preregistration/Dataverse pointers were recorded as pointers only, not evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, figure notes, and footnotes received identical evidentiary status. A display earned credit when it supplied the required information; supplementary-table pointers supplied no omitted information.
findings: Figures 1–7 and their notes earned criterion 16 credit because they display OLS point estimates and 95% confidence intervals.
Those same notes did not earn criteria 7, 10, 11, 14, or 17 because they omit the complete model, specification, dependence adjustment, and per-analysis N.
The claim that unadjusted marginal means are reported was checked against Figures 2–7; the displays are baseline-normalized coefficient plots, so criterion 15 remains 0.

Figure 3 is titled Warmth but its note says perceived legitimacy; the title, surrounding prose, and survey description support interpretation as warmth, while the note inconsistency is retained as an audit finding.
Selected prose confidence intervals on printed 391 and 393 sometimes present endpoints in descending order; they were treated as reported uncertainty, not silently corrected.
Every supplementary-material pointer was treated only as evidence that the main article defers detail, never as evidence that the detail is present.

direct_comparison.interpretation: The main article is strongest on analysis units, coding, clustered uncertainty, numerical effects, traceability, and validity-threat discussion. It is weakest on reproducible recruitment and intervention/control details, random-sequence generation, complete outcome construction, full flow, complete covariates, missing outcomes, multiplicity/status, raw group quantities, and self-contained robustness evidence.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables and table/figure notes were given the same evidentiary status as prose. Tables 1–4 earned credit for analysis units, sample sizes, estimates, standard errors, clustering, fixed effects, and column mapping where their notes supplied those facts. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, vague 'controls' labels and pointers to SI did not supply omitted covariate identities, outcome components, or robustness results.

Figure 3 visually inspected and confirmed as an alignment comparison rather than a randomized vignette contrast

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent session; no cross-paper ranking is possible here.

findings: Figures 4–10 and every figure note were read as evidence on the same footing as prose.
Figure labels earned credit for raw outcome coding and group percentages.
Figure notes earned credit for naming OLS and the displayed uncertainty levels, but not for unreported SE/CI construction.
Appendix pointers on pages 795–796 were not treated as supplying omitted eligibility, sampling, or procedural details.
No regression equation was demanded; the scores reflect whether the figures, notes, and prose jointly made implementation unambiguous.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. additional_checklist.note: No additional reporting checklist was supplied; no checklist assessment was performed.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is pending.

rows.summary: The main article identifies the randomized contrast and two estimators, but omits exact instruments, randomization generation, Lin specification, focal N, arm means, and explicit uncertainty construction.

findings: Main-text prose, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status.
Figure 6 and its note were used positively for the displayed estimators and outward appendix pointer; the pointer itself did not supply excluded model details.
The plotted DiM point and intervals were not treated as exact numerical values or labeled confidence intervals because the display and note do not provide those labels.
No regression equation was demanded; the score reflects whether prose plus displays jointly made implementation reconstructable.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

title: Deliberation and Ethical Voting Behavior: Evidence from a Campaign Experiment in Benin

reviewed_pages.boundary_confirmation: All 17 PDF pages are the published main article. PDF pp. 1–15 contain article text through the Supplementary Material availability notice; PDF pp. 16–17 contain declarations and references. No appendix is embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only, including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Supplementary material, Dataverse, external links, and referenced results outside the article were not used as evidence.

experiments.name: 2011 Benin village-level town-hall campaign experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: A new village-level randomized assignment (60 town-hall villages, 90 usual-campaign controls) tests substantive effects on administrative and survey outcomes; this is the article's central experiment.

design_map.label: Target population
design_map.value: Eligible voters/citizens in sampled villages across 30 communes in 11 Beninese provinces, concentrated in the assigned candidates’ regional strongholds; the main article does not state a single formal target-population definition.

evidence.anchor: 150 randomly selected villages
evidence.paraphrase: The intervention is described as a 150-village experiment with 60 town-hall villages and 90 usual-campaign villages.

evidence.anchor: randomized geographical block design
evidence.paraphrase: Thirty communes were selected across 11 provinces after excluding Cotonou; five villages per commune were selected, two treated and three control.

design_map.label: Eligibility criteria
design_map.value: NR

evidence.paraphrase: The Sampling and Data and Estimation sections call survey respondents prospective voters but do not state respondent age, voter-registration, residence-duration, village-frame, or other eligibility rules.

design_map.label: Recruitment procedure
design_map.value: Communes were selected with a random-number generator after geographic exclusions/proportional allocation; five villages per commune were randomly selected. Survey respondents were recruited by a random walk from the village center, with quotas of 40 in treated and 30 in control villages.

evidence.anchor: randomized geographical block design
evidence.paraphrase: Thirty communes were selected across 11 provinces after excluding Cotonou; five villages per commune were selected, two treated and three control.

evidence.anchor: random walk procedure

design_map.label: Field dates and setting
design_map.value: Benin, 2011 presidential campaign: policy conference February 5; town halls February 20–March 6; election March 13; post-election survey March 14–31.

evidence.anchor: March 14 ... until March 31

design_map.label: Number recruited and analyzed

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison because this independent session contains one paper.
direct_comparison.finding: The three primary country experiments have identical main-article transparency: estimands and respondent analysis units are identifiable, but allocation, coding, complete model implementation, inference, analysis Ns, raw quantities, and exact numerical uncertainty are not reconstructable. consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figures earned credit for displaying outcome/contrast mappings and plotted effects, while their notes did not earn missing model or inference details when they only pointed to excluded supplementary material.

checks.finding: Used as evidence for outcomes, contrasts, and plotted country-specific results; not treated as supplying exact estimates, interval definitions, sample sizes, or full models that are absent from the display.
Used for OLS, pooled ATE, and covariates; not treated as fully specifying country models, coding, transformations, or inference.
Used for reported sample counts and limitations; pointers to Appendix/Dataverse were not treated as evidence of omitted content.
The stated overall 4,754 conflicts with footnote country counts totaling 4,554; neither was silently preferred.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. rows.assessment: Highest statistical traceability: equation, Table 4, N, OLS coefficients, robust SE, and mapped marginal effects. Still not fully reproducible because allocation, exact stimuli, flow, robust-SE variant, missingness, multiplicity, and scope limits are absent.
Closely matches Study 3 and has the same strengths and gaps; Table 5 and Figure 5 map results clearly.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were assigned equal evidentiary status. Tables 4–5 and their notes earned credit for OLS, N, estimates, and robust-SE labeling; Figure notes earned model-to-result mapping credit. Credit was withheld only where these displays and prose jointly remained incomplete. Appendix/SI and Dataverse pointers were not treated as evidence. One apparent source-level arithmetic/sign discrepancy was preserved: page 8 states MLatinos − MAsians = −0.307, although the displayed means 0.472 and 0.164 imply +0.308 (rounding). This does not alter the reconstructability scores.
examples: Table 4 note supports Study 3 estimator, N, and robust-SE label.
Table 5 note supports Study 4 estimator, N, and robust-SE label.
Figure 4/5 notes support linkage of marginal effects to Tables 4/5, but do not state interval level or construction.

findings: Figure 1, Figure 2, Table 1, its note, Equations 1–2, and footnotes were treated as evidence on the same basis as prose.
Equation 1 earned direct-model credit and Equation 2 earned list-model credit because the operations and coding they show are reconstructable.
Table 1 earned credit for sample sizes, estimates, control quantities, and model-to-column mapping.

Appendix pointers for cleaning, diagnostics, balance, ordered probit, clustering, covariates, and maximum-likelihood analyses were recorded as pointers only, not as supplied evidence.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes received identical evidentiary status. Tables 2–5 earned credit wherever their labels and notes supplied information. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, appendix pointers supplied no credit. Table 4's visible title says 'Studies 3 and 4' while adjacent prose describes pooling the two preceding experiments (Studies 2 and 3); this inconsistency was retained as a traceability limitation.

items.example: Tables 2–3 establish OLS, variables, coefficients, SEs, Ns, scaling, and two-tailed thresholds.
Figure 4's note establishes medsens() and 1,000 simulations.
Footnotes 6–7 inform screening robustness and the ceiling-effect discussion.
SM.5–SM.8 pointers do not supply omitted stimuli, items, exclusions, or computations.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

statistical_transparency_comparison: Within this one-paper assessment, the U.S. and Canadian experiments have nearly identical statistical reporting. The Canadian experiment is one design item less complete because its real Indigenous-group levels are withheld, and its Canadian-only STM adds an unreconstructable focal model. No between-paper comparison is possible in this independent single-paper session.

findings: Main-text figures and notes were treated as evidence on the same footing as prose.
Figure 1 supplied randomized levels and factorial structure; Figures 2–4 and 6 supplied displayed estimates, labels, sample counts, and visible error bars where present.

No credit was withheld merely because information appeared in a display note; conversely, pointers from those notes to supplementary tables did not supply omitted SEs, model specifications, or confidence-interval construction.
Visual inspection of PDF pages 8–14 resolved figure labels and error bars that plain-text extraction could not fully preserve.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, Figure 4 and its note, Table 3 and its note, and footnotes 22–23 received the same evidentiary status. Table 3 earned credit for its explicit respondent clustering, sample size, estimates, and standard errors. Figure 4 earned evidence credit for displayed marginal means and 95% intervals, but not for exact numerical values or an unreported CI procedure. Pointers to Supplementary Tables A17–A23 and the preregistration were treated only as evidence that details were omitted from the main article, not as evidence for their contents.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

title: When Are Legislators Responsive to Ethnic Minorities? Testing the Role of Electoral Incentives and Candidate Selection for Mitigating Ethnocentric Responsiveness
boundary_finding: The PDF contains exactly the 17 published article pages, beginning with title/abstract on printed p. 450 and ending with references on p. 466. The supplementary-material notice on p. 465 is only a pointer; no supplement is embedded.
source_scope: Published main article only, including main-text prose, tables, figures, notes, and footnotes on PDF pp. 1–17 (printed pp. 450–466). Online appendices, preregistration content, Dataverse, code, and external references were not consulted and do not supply omitted information.
scope_exclusion_summary: No list-experiment measurement designs were identified; therefore no design was excluded under the current list-experiment restriction.

experiments.name: 2017 Danish municipal-politician factorial email audit
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment: the article's central 2×2×2 randomized field audit jointly assigns requester ethnicity, requester gender, and an explicit personal-vote cue to a new email sample and formally analyzes reply outcomes.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment-level comparison; cross-paper synthesis is deferred because this session assesses one paper.
direct_comparison.summary: The two primary experiments have essentially identical reporting: conditions, outcomes, linear-model family, covariates, and treatment coefficients are visible, but analysis N and inference procedures are not. The August diagnostic is more transparent about raw means, effects, and SEs, while still omitting analysis N and SE construction. The national-identity timing diagnostic is least reconstructable because only a qualitative null is in the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, figure labels, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figures 1–2 received credit for visible coefficient labels, reference categories, and model correspondence. They did not receive inferred credit for interval type, confidence level, SE estimator, clustering, or analysis N because those are not stated. Figure 4 was recognized as graphing arm quantities but did not earn full group-quantity credit because exact values and arm N are absent. Appendix pointers supplied no evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

direct_comparison.scope_note: This independent session contains one paper, so cross-paper ranking is not possible. The comparison below is between its scored experiments; later synthesis can compare validated paper records.
direct_comparison.finding: Study 1 reports outcome-level AMCE figures and respondent clustering but omits most non-governance levels and complete model implementations. Study 2 more clearly states its pooled OLS operation and raw condition means, but omits exact frame text, allocation details, arm Ns, and contrast CIs.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given identical evidentiary status. Figure 3 earned evidence for effects, reference condition, clustering, and interval levels; Figure 4 for named estimators/bootstrap draws; Figure 6 and its note for group means, dates, N, and bootstrap intervals. No score was reduced because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose. Conversely, display labels and estimator names did not receive credit for unreported probabilities, coding, model implementation, or interval construction. Pointers to supplementary tables/figures were treated only as evidence that information was absent from the permitted source.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. Figure 1 and Table 3 earned credit for displayed estimates/CIs. Appendix pointers earned no credit for omitted content.

direct_comparison.summary: Only one paper is in scope, so no cross-paper ranking is possible. Within this article, the sole scored supporting experiment reports effects, standard errors, and analysis Ns but does not make the estimator, covariate blocks, randomization implementation, or missing-data flow reconstructable. Observational analyses are inventoried but not scored as experiments.

findings: Table 2 and its note received the same evidentiary status as prose: they earned credit for outcome identification, coefficients, robust-SE labeling, observation counts, pooled means, specification-block indicators, and the attentive-subset rule.
Credit was withheld only where the combined prose/table record remained incomplete: estimator, covariate identities, robust-SE variant, arm-specific quantities, and flow counts.
Footnote 21’s pointer to Supporting Information was recorded but did not supply the omitted survey wording.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figures, table/figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 3 supplied means and n; Figure 4 and its note supplied SE-bar and t-test information; Tables 5–6 supplied outcomes, coefficients, parenthetical uncertainty, and n. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, display labels did not receive credit for unreported implementation details, and pointers to supplementary appendices were not treated as evidence.
examples: Table 3 and Figure 4 were credited for group means, sample size, SE bars and reported t-test thresholds.
Table 5 was credited for OLS outcome, regressors, column changes, coefficients and sample sizes.
Tables 5–6 did not earn unreported SE-estimator, clustering or dependence details.
Supplement-only Appendix A/C/D/E/F pointers supplied no omitted content.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

direct_comparison.scope_note: This independent session contains one paper; cross-paper synthesis is reserved for the later validated synthesis. The comparison below is therefore between its separately scored experiments.
direct_comparison.finding: Both experiments disclose analysis units, plotted effects/uncertainty, and inferential-scope limits, but neither fully reports the assignment probabilities, full treatment levels, model coding, missing-data rules, multiplicity, or exact N for every focal model. E2 names OLS and country fixed effects more explicitly than E1 names its AMCE implementation, but criterion 7 remains 0 for both because E2 omits numeric outcome and regressor/reference coding.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given identical evidentiary status. Figure notes earned credit for respondent clustering, confidence intervals, fixed effects, and sample sizes. No score was reduced because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose. Conversely, figure pointers to Supplementary Material did not supply omitted models, treatment levels, robustness results, or coding.
examples: Figures 3–7 and their notes support effects, 95% CIs, clustering, and displayed sample counts.
Figure 2 and its note support the attribute families and paired presentation.
Pointers to Supplementary Material §§A, C, E–N were treated as absence in the main article, not evidence.

direct_comparison.scope_note: This independent session contains one paper, so no cross-paper winner or ranking is possible. The table compares its two experiments; cross-paper synthesis is reserved for later validated records.
direct_comparison.finding: The two experiments have the same core-item profile because they share the randomization and modeling framework. MFV has stronger country breadth; MFQ has no missing outcomes, but neither difference resolves the common reconstruction gaps.

findings: Main-text equations and Figures 3–6, including captions and notes, received the same evidentiary status as prose.
Figure-displayed estimates and intervals earned criterion 16 credit even where redundant prose was absent.
Figure notes were not penalized for being notes; conversely, they could not supply omitted interval construction, repeated-observation handling, subgroup sample sizes, or full stimuli.
Pointers to Supplementary Table 1, Appendices A2/A7, and replication materials were recorded as pointers only and supplied no evidence.
No main-text regression table was present; the article's equations and graphical model outputs were assessed under the same reconstructability rule.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. consistency_audit.finding: Prose, equations, Tables 1–2 and their notes, Figures 2–6 and their notes, and footnotes were all treated as eligible main-article evidence. Table 1 earned full conditions credit. Table 2 earned credit for its displayed analysis Ns, covariate rows, outcomes, and maximum–minimum interpretation. Figure 2 earned point-estimate evidence but not inference credit because its interval bars and note do not identify the interval type, level, or construction. Pointers to supplementary tables/sections did not supply omitted details.

checks.example: Equations 1–2 and surrounding definitions supported estimand, unit, and coding judgments.
Table 1 fully established list contents; Table 2 established multivariable Ns and displayed marginal-effect interpretation.

Footnote 11 established that a preregistration existed, but not analysis-by-analysis status.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment-level comparison; cross-paper synthesis is deferred because this independent session contains one paper.
direct_comparison.summary: All three studies clearly report assignment and arm-level outcomes. Study 3 is statistically most traceable because it names ITT, CACE, the sharp null, the ri package, and test sidedness, but it still omits the exact randomization-inference implementation and all SEs/CIs. Studies 1–2 omit sufficient variance/test details to reproduce their p values; Study 1 also omits numerical pairwise effect estimates.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, tables, table/figure notes, footnotes, and the article’s printed Appendix A were given identical evidentiary status. Figure 1 and Figure 2 notes supplied arm n values and ±1 SE descriptions; Tables 1–2 and the Table 2 note supplied Study 3 flow, estimates, p values, N, and the named inference approach. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display, and no appendix pointer was treated as evidence for excluded material.

additional_checklist.note: No additional reporting checklist was supplied, so no separate checklist assessment was performed.

direct_comparison: All three parallel country experiments have the same criterion totals and nearly identical reporting structure. The U.S. experiment has one additional allocation-probability omission for its four-level randomized office attribute; this does not change the already-zero randomization criterion. Main-text figures are unusually traceable for effects, samples, and clustered uncertainty, while exact weighted-model reproduction and flow/missingness remain impossible from the main article alone.

findings: Main-text figures, captions, figure notes, Table 1, table notes, footnotes, and prose were given equal evidentiary status.
Figure notes earned credit for estimator family, sample sizes, confidence level, and clustering; no penalty was imposed merely because information appeared in a display rather than prose.
The integrated article appendix on PDF page 11 was treated as main-article evidence. Pointers to Tables A1–A12 in the Online Appendix were not treated as supplying their omitted content.

Graphical point estimates and confidence intervals counted as reported effects and uncertainty; unavailable exact weight construction, CI formula, and online-only coefficient tables were not inferred.

experiments.classification_rationale: Analysis of measured pathogen disgust and conservatism in a representative U.S. sample; no randomization is reported.

direct_comparison.summary: Within this one-paper assessment, both experiments provide traceable regression estimates in main-text tables, but neither fully reports random assignment, participant flow, missingness, multiplicity, or inferential scope. E1 is clearer on treatment/outcome coding; E2 is clearer on factorial levels and figure-to-table mapping. Their criterion totals are identical, though the specific omissions differ.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables, table notes, figure notes, prose, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 3 earned model, sample-size, effect, and inference credit; Table 4 and Figure 1 earned corresponding credit. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display, and appendix pointers were not treated as evidence for omitted details.
examples: Table 3 plus its note supports E1 criteria 7, 14, 16, and 17.
Table 4 plus its note and Figure 1 note support E2 criteria 7, 14, 16, and 17.
Table 1 supports population/recruitment evidence but not unreported eligibility or exclusions.

title: Voter Registration Costs and Disenfranchisement: Experimental Evidence from France

reviewed_pages.statement: All 21 PDF pages were reviewed. The article starts on PDF page 1/printed page 584 and ends on PDF page 21/printed page 604; no appendix is embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only: body text, Figures 1–6 and notes, Tables 1–4 and notes, and footnotes on PDF pages 1–21. Online appendices A–G and all external materials were excluded.
ai_notice: AI-generated reporting judgments await human review.
inventory_notes: One distinct randomized field experiment was identified. All six arms and later administrative/survey follow-ups reuse the same assignment. No embedded list experiment, separate diagnostic randomization, pilot without outcome, or article-authored observational study was identified.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, tables, figures, footnotes, and their notes were given the same evidentiary status when present in the main article. direct_comparison.summary: Strongest transparency: outcomes, analysis unit, school-clustered inference, sample sizes, effect estimates, and scope caveats. Principal reconstruction barriers: recruitment/eligibility, randomization generation and allocation, control condition, treatment receipt coding, flow to N=812, weighting status, multiplicity/status, raw-mean contradiction, and main-text robustness detail.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 and its note earned credit for covariates, fixed effects, clustering, confidence intervals, sample sizes, model labels, effects, and uncertainty. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, table labels such as TOT and tobit did not cure missing operational coding. Appendix pointers were treated only as evidence of main-article absence.

single_paper_comparison_note: This session contains one paper, so no between-paper ranking is possible. P108's strongest statistical-transparency features are Equation 1 and Table 3's outcome/treatment/robust-SE mapping. Its main reconstructability gaps are allocation and flow, outcome coding, exact adjusted-model specifications, within-respondent dependence handling, analysis-specific Ns, and resampling/CI implementation. Cross-paper synthesis is reserved for the later independent-assessment stage.

findings: Table 1 and its note jointly earned criterion 2 credit for the two domains and five elicitation types.
Table 2 and its note supplied the analyzed arm counts and clarified that its final column is a t statistic; realized counts were not misread as allocation probabilities.
Equation 1 plus Table 3 and its note earned credit for the bivariate OLS mapping and heteroskedastic-robust standard errors.
Figure notes were credited for coefficient, interval, seating-percentage, and predictive-error mappings where explicit.
Neither prose nor tables received inferred credit for unreported covariates, matching/weight construction, respondent clustering, analysis Ns, or confidence-interval construction.
Pointers to supplementary material on PDF pp. 4–6, 9, 11, 13, 15, 18–19 were recorded as absences, not evidence that omitted details were reported.

direct_comparison.interpretation: The main article is strongest on exact treatment materials, explicit OLS equations/tables, sample size, estimates, and table-to-text mapping. Its largest reconstructability gaps are random-sequence generation, participant flow, complete covariate/reference coding, missingness/attrition accounting, multiplicity/status, arm-specific raw outcomes, and several internal-validity threats.

No credit was awarded for details merely pointed to in Online Appendix A/B or external cited work.

experiments.classification_rationale: Observational ecological analysis relating 2012 Democratic vote share to 2015 marketplace enrollment; no randomized assignment.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper session; comparison is between the two scored experiments, not a cross-paper ranking.
direct_comparison.finding: The primary field experiment is materially more transparent than the supporting MTurk experiment: Table 1 and Figures 4–5 identify effects, subgroup samples, arm quantities, and clustered uncertainty. Even so, the field estimator, allocation probabilities, exact randomized count, confidence-interval construction, and analysis-status/multiplicity rules remain unreconstructable. The MTurk experiment mainly reports directions and p-values and omits nearly all implementation details needed to reproduce its analyses.

findings: Prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as equally eligible evidence.
Table 1 received credit for treatment direction, outcome, subgroup Ns, coefficients, robust standard errors, ZIP-code clustering, and mode-specific sample differences.
Figures 4–5 received credit for arm quantities, subgroup Ns, and 95% confidence intervals; visual inspection confirmed the display notes and Table 1 parentheses.
No credit was withheld merely because information appeared in a display, and no appendix pointer was treated as supplying omitted information.

inventory_note: Nine original randomized experiments were identified: seven persuasion canvass experiments, one North Carolina turnout experiment with a reported outcome, and one Missouri turnout diagnostic experiment with no main-article outcome. The North Carolina literature drop uses the same randomized assignment as the North Carolina persuasion experiment and is not a new experiment. No sensitive-item/item-count list experiment appears in the main article. The 40 prior studies are analyzed as a meta-analysis and are not individually reported sufficiently in the main article to inventory as article experiments.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: Within this paper, all seven persuasion experiments share the same reporting strengths (estimand, analysis unit, coding, estimates/SEs) and the same principal gaps (allocation, exact scripts/placebo, covariate list, counts, attrition, multiplicity, and CI construction). The North Carolina turnout experiment is less transparent because it lacks an explicit estimand, SE/CI, and detailed outcome/model reporting; the Missouri diagnostic is least transparent because no outcome result is reported.

findings: Table 2 and its row labels/notes were credited exactly like prose for experiment identity, timing, race, estimates, and standard errors.
Figure 4 was credited for its displayed meta-analytic quantities but not used to fill missing experiment-level counts or specifications.
Footnotes were credited as main-article evidence (including CACE/TOT in footnote 22 and the Missouri turnout experiment in footnote 19).
Pointers to Online Appendix D were recorded as pointers only and supplied no credit for omitted scripts, balance, attrition, dates, question wording, or sample counts.
The same binary evidentiary standard was applied to every scored experiment; common reporting produced common scores, while the turnout experiment differed only where its reporting differed.

consistency_audit.finding: Prose, figures, figure notes, tables, table notes, and footnotes were treated as evidence under the same standard.
Figure notes earned credit for displayed analysis Ns and 95% CI bars, but visual CI bars for group means were not converted into unreported treatment-effect CIs.
Table 1 and Table 2 were credited for recruitment/sample facts but not for unreported module-specific allocation and flow.
Pointers to the Supplementary Material and Dataverse were recorded as absences, not as supplied evidence.
No regression equation was demanded redundantly; model credit failed because main-text displays and notes did not jointly disclose the focal specifications.

direct_comparison_note: Single-paper session: the comparison table contrasts the four experiment-level records. Cross-paper synthesis is intentionally deferred.

Graphical estimates and intervals earned Criterion 16 credit. Pointers to the Online Appendix supplied no credit.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

title: Can Social Contact Reduce Prejudice and Discrimination? Evidence from a Field Experiment in Nigeria
source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–24 (printed pp. 654–677), including main-text figures, tables, notes, and footnotes. Online appendices, registry, replication files, and external references were not used as evidence.

main_article_boundary.finding: The supplied 24-page PDF is the complete main article; references begin on PDF p. 22. It contains no appended supplement. Appendix mentions are pointers only.

inventory_notes: No conventional list experiment is reported in the main article.
The random laptop raffle is an attendance incentive, not a research manipulation with a reported outcome, and is not inventoried as an experiment.
Sampling randomization and the small additional Christian recruitment draw are recruitment operations, not distinct outcome experiments.
No category 3 diagnostic randomization, category 4 pilot with no reported outcome, or category 5 observational analysis was identified within the stated experimental scope.
