direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper comparison is not possible at this stage.
direct_comparison.summary: Within P117, all three experiments have explicit OLS models, analysis units, coding, clustered/robust uncertainty, sample sizes, and model-to-result links. Reconstructability is reduced consistently by absent sequence generation, absent primary/secondary outcome labels, incomplete missing-data rules, and absent multiplicity/status mapping. The dictator experiment uniquely reports raw arm/group quantities; the destruction experiment does not.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment comparison only; cross-paper synthesis is deferred because this independent session contains one paper.
direct_comparison.finding: All three administrations use the same well-described profile conditions and identifiable profile-rating unit. Statistical results are pooled across survey sources, so none has an administration-specific estimand, N, effect, uncertainty estimate, raw arm means, or fully specified dependence procedure. The national administration reports more recruitment information (2,000 opt-in U.S. adults) than either minority administration, but all three receive the same criterion totals.

consistency_audit.finding: Prose, Table 2, Figure 1, Figure 2, footnotes, and display notes were given the same evidentiary status. Table 2 earned full conditions credit; Figures 1–2 earned evidence credit for pooled effects/interval levels and subgroup dimensions. Appendix pointers were recorded only as proof that main-article information was absent, never as evidence that omitted values were reported.

This independent session contains one paper; validated cross-paper synthesis is reserved for the later synthesis stage.

findings: Tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were given the same evidentiary status as prose.
Table 2 received credit for its explicit outcome, logit estimator, covariate changes, reference categories, coefficients, and column sample sizes.
Table 2 did not receive inferred credit for an unlabeled parenthetical uncertainty estimator, clustering, repeated-observation adjustment, weights, or confidence-interval construction.
Footnote 11 received credit for the reported round-order percentages and t statistics, but not for unreported position-specific Ns or an inference recipe.
Pointers to Tables A.1–A.9 and supplementary material were not treated as evidence that omitted information was reported.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.summary: E1 is substantially more statistically transparent because Table 1 and its note identify OLS, covariates, sample sizes, robust SEs, and cluster levels. E2 reports raw means and p<.01 but omits the test, uncertainty magnitude, dependence adjustment, and analyzed condition counts. E3 is only a footnote-level robustness report and is not statistically reconstructable.

findings: Table 1 and its note received the same evidentiary status as prose: they earned estimator, sample-size, uncertainty, and clustering credit where complete.
Figures 4–6 and Table 2 were credited for quantities they visibly report, but not for absent sample counts or inferential procedures.
Footnotes 15–26 and 29–32 were treated as main-article evidence. Appendix/supplement pointers were not treated as supplying omitted information.
No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display or note rather than prose.

findings: The corrected sentence, Table 2, and Table 2 note were treated as equal evidentiary sources.
Criterion 2 received full credit from the corrected sentence plus Table 2 and its note; prose was not privileged over the display.

The table note supplied the control identity and fixed-last restriction, while unreported probabilities, sequence-generation details, outcomes, sample sizes, models, and results received no inferred credit.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

title: The Informational Theory of Legislative Committees: An Experimental Analysis

reviewed_pages.boundary_basis: The PDF begins with the article title on PDF p. 1/printed p. 55 and ends with references on PDF p. 22/printed p. 76. The supplementary-material and replication notices on PDF p. 22 are links only; no appendix or supplement pages are embedded.

source_scope: Only the supplied published main article, including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Online appendices, replication materials, and all linked external content were excluded.
inventory_notes: Two scored randomized experiments were identified: one primary main-treatment experiment and one diagnostic robustness experiment. The six main cells and eight robustness cells are arms within those two experiment programs. No list experiment, unreported-outcome pilot, or observational analysis was found.

direct_comparison.note: Within this one-paper session, comparison is across experiment classes. E1 provides substantially more statistical transparency than E2: E1 supplies model tables, Ns, raw session quantities, and inference labels, whereas E2 largely supplies a qualitative preservation table and appendix pointers. Cross-paper synthesis is reserved for the later independent-assessment stage.

findings: Main-text tables and their notes were treated as evidence with the same status as prose.
Criteria 9, 10, 14, 15, and 17 received credit in E1 where Tables 3–8 and notes supplied coding, specifications, Ns, raw quantities, or traceability.
No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a table.
Conversely, Table 9 did not receive model-reconstruction credit because it contains only preservation categories and expressly sends supporting analysis to online Appendix B.
Appendix pointers in footnotes 14, 21, 22, 25, 29, and 31 were recorded as absences, not as supplied evidence.

direct_comparison.finding: The list experiment is materially more statistically reconstructable: its estimator, arm means, effect, SEs, and office-clustered tests are explicit. The communications experiment states its vignette and outcomes precisely but omits exact result Ns, full specification, SE/CI, and dependence/test procedures.

consistency_audit.finding: Prose, figure text, footnotes, and display notes were given equal evidentiary status. The only randomized results are in prose and footnotes; no regression table was penalized for being a table, and no appendix pointer was counted as evidence.
checks: Figure 1 and footnote 9 were used only for what they report (survey balance and office clustering for that figure), not silently extended to experiment-specific inference.
Footnote 27 was credited as evidence of office-clustered testing for the list experiment.
Footnotes 26 and 30 were treated as appendix pointers, not as evidence that robustness details appeared in the main article.
Narrative numerical results on pp. 14–15 received the same status a table cell and note would receive.

direct_comparison.statistical_transparency: Within P134, Tables 1–3 are materially more reconstructable than Figures 1–2. The tables report numerical coefficients, clustered standard errors and observation counts (and some control means), whereas the figures omit numerical estimates, analysis Ns, and the definition of uncertainty bars. The AES formula, covariates, weights, fixed effects, and clustering are reported, but constituent outcomes/coding and the underlying non-crime outcome estimator are incomplete.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status when they were inside the main article. Table notes earned credit for clustered SEs, sample restrictions, Ns, and control means. Figure notes were also used, but did not earn information they did not state. Appendix pointers and external citations were not treated as supplying omitted information.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment-level comparison (cross-paper synthesis is deferred).
direct_comparison.finding: The primary marijuana PICA experiment is substantially more transparent than the three supporting replications, which are only named in a footnote and deferred to excluded Appendix E. Even the primary experiment is not fully reconstructable because stimuli, flow/analysis counts, missing-data rules, complete outcome coding, weights/adjustments, and general inference construction are absent.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figure notes, and footnotes were given the same evidentiary status. Graphical point estimates and confidence intervals earned results credit; Figure 3's note earned estimator/contrast credit; footnote 24 earned credit only for the pooled-SE calculation it actually describes. No regression table appears in the main article. Appendix pointers and citations did not supply omitted methods.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, figure labels, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Figure 1 supplied arm/subgroup counts and graphical confidence intervals; Figures 2–5 supplied estimate type and interval levels; footnotes 2–11 supplied panel, coding, covariate, and appendix-pointer information. Appendix pointers were treated only as evidence that information was absent from the main article, never as evidence that the omitted information was reported.

source_scope: Published main article only: all text, main tables/figures, notes, and footnotes on PDF pp. 1–17 (printed 963–979). Online appendices, supplementary materials, replication files, external links, and cited methods were excluded as evidence.

evidence.anchor: average marginal effect ... based on probit estimations

additional_checklist.reason: No additional reporting checklist was supplied; no separate checklist was created.

consistency_audit.finding: Main-text prose, equations, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as equally eligible evidence. Table 2 earned credit for sample sizes, observed quantities, the exact-binomial test, and Holm–Bonferroni adjustment; it did not earn unreported standard errors or confidence intervals. Appendix pointers supplied no omitted evidence.

records.anchor: Absolute (N) and Relative Frequency (N%) of Participants Who Cast Distance-Minimizing Votes
records.paraphrase: Table 2 reports arm and pooled sample sizes, counts, percentages, expected percentages, and adjusted significance stars for all three distance scales.

records.anchor: Notches represent non-parametric estimates of 95% confidence intervals for the medians
records.paraphrase: Figure 1 displays pooled placement distributions, medians, means, and 95% intervals, but does not state the mean-interval construction or an analysis N in the figure.

records.anchor: 97 participants were assigned to the delay version, of which eight finished wave 1, but failed to complete wave 2
records.paraphrase: The delayed arm lost eight of 97 between waves, leaving 89 complete cases and 393 complete experimental responses overall.
The exact candidate statements are not in the main article; page 286 explicitly points to Table A.2 in excluded online supplementary materials.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is not possible in this session.
direct_comparison.finding: Within P138, the primary experiment is more statistically transparent than the embedded label randomization: the primary analysis identifies its descriptive estimand, exact-binomial test, arm samples, observed proportions, null quantities, and multiplicity adjustment, whereas the label randomization reports no estimand, model, sample, or result.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; no cross-paper ranking is possible. The table compares the paper’s scored experiments without averaging classes.
direct_comparison.finding: All three experiments share the same major transparency strengths (arm counts, respondent analysis unit, household clustering, standardized effects and graphical uncertainty) and the same major reconstruction barriers (exact scripts, complete outcomes/coding, covariate identities, missingness rules, and focal analysis Ns). Experiment 3 additionally lacks an unambiguous telephone-specific estimand.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1, Figures 1–3, and all display notes received equal evidentiary status. Table 1 earned credit for arm content, ITT definition, effects, and CACE explanation; figure notes earned credit for contrasts, primary status, respondent-level pooling, and uncertainty. They did not earn credit for information they do not contain. Appendix pointers supplied no omitted evidence.

experiments.name: Lucid 2024 foreign-electoral-intervention factorial vignette experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment: one sample of 3,510 U.S. adults received one randomized vignette. components.label: Noncompliance
components.rationale: Post-treatment inattentiveness is measured, retained in ITT, and examined with a stated exclusion threshold in sensitivity analysis.

evidence.anchor: “include all 3,510 people who took our survey”

evidence.anchor: “excluded subjects who answered less than 80% of the checks correctly”

components.label: Spillovers
components.rationale: A one-person, one-vignette online survey has no clustered treatment setting or interaction through which experimental spillovers are logically part of the design.
components.missing: Logically inapplicable to the individually delivered, single-session vignette design described on PDF pp. 6–7.

components.label: Demand effects
components.rationale: The article does not discuss whether scenario wording, obvious hypotheses, or repeated attitudinal questions cued responses.
components.missing: Absent: demand-characteristic, hypothesis-guessing, or experimenter-expectancy discussion. Reviewed Research Design, Findings, and Conclusion on PDF pp. 6–16.

components.label: Measurement problems
components.rationale: The paper notes hypothetical context but does not assess reliability, social desirability, dichotomization loss, or validity of stated policy support.
components.missing: Absent: direct discussion of outcome reliability/validity, social desirability, hypothetical bias, or consequences of binary recoding. Reviewed PDF pp. 8–16.

components.label: Other relevant threats
components.rationale: The article discusses treatment realism, ambiguity, 2016 context, partisan messaging, and generalization to other settings.

evidence.anchor: “Our scenarios conveyed no ambiguity about whether the foreign country tampered”

evidence.anchor: “events of 2016 might have affected average disapproval”

evidence.anchor: “future research could explore the effects … in other countries”

evidence.anchor: “taking attitudes … in each treatment condition and subtracting … the baseline condition”

findings: Table 1 received full evidentiary credit for randomized attributes, levels, and cross-arm restrictions.

direct_comparison.summary: The video study identifies its estimators more clearly (OLS, random-effects GLS, autoregressive random-effects) than the photo study, while both clearly report analysis units, focal estimates, uncertainty, and pooled model Ns. Neither study fully reports recruitment, randomization probabilities/sequence generation, exact stimulus implementation, missing-data flow, or inference/dependence construction. The photo study uniquely acknowledges untestable carryover from always following the video study.
direct_comparison.winner: No cross-paper ranking is possible in this one-paper independent assessment; experiment-level differences are reported without averaging.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, figures, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 2–6 estimates, standard errors, Ns, headings, and notes received credit wherever they resolved a component. Scores were not reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Appendix pointers received no credit for omitted detail.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, figures, figure notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Figures 1–9 and their notes were credited for the outcomes, contrasts, qualitative group patterns, and p-values they actually show. They were not credited for numeric means/effects, analysis Ns, model specifications, or inference procedures that are absent or deferred to excluded appendices. No criterion was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.
